open_points.subject: OwnerFormField submitted-name collisions
open_points.question: Must submitted field names be unique, and if so is uniqueness global or separate for each carrier; what required refusal occurs when the release contains a collision?
options: Require names to be globally unique and reject a release containing duplicates.
Require names to be unique only within each OwnerFormCarrier and allow the same name in different carriers.
Allow duplicate names and define deterministic handling of every matching row.
open_points.default_guess: Require names to be globally unique and reject the release before it is used.

witness.initial: A release contains two OwnerFormField rows named `amount`, one carried by the request and one by its values.
events: The form reader resolves the submitted name against the release table.
outcomes: The reader rejects the release or submission because `amount` is not unique.
The reader accepts the entry and applies it to one or both rows because carriers form separate namespaces.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal or sees the value assigned to a different part of the request.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField name equality
open_points.question: What equality rules apply to field names, including case, Unicode normalization, and leading or trailing whitespace, both for lookup and for collision detection?
options: Names are compared as exact code-point strings.
Names are normalized and/or case-folded before comparison.
Only a restricted canonical name syntax is allowed, and noncanonical names are refused.
open_points.default_guess: Require a restricted canonical name syntax and compare canonical strings exactly.

witness.initial: The release contains a field named `Email`.
events: The owner submits a field named `email`.
The form reader matches submitted names to OwnerFormField rows.
outcomes: The submission is refused because names are case-sensitive.
The submission is accepted because names are compared case-insensitively.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus acceptance.

open_points.subject: closed-list OwnerFormField values
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Where is the closed list for a field defined, how are submitted values matched to it, and what required result or refusal applies to a value outside it?
options: Each closed-list field identifies its own allowed-value set, and values outside that set are refused.
FormValueKind identifies a shared closed set, and values outside that set are refused.
The list is supplied by another release table keyed by field name, with a defined result when the key or list is missing.
open_points.default_guess: Give each closed-list field an explicit reference to a release-owned allowed-value set and refuse values not in that set.

witness.initial: A release has a `colour` field whose reads_as value means closed list, but the supplied facts name no permitted choices.
events: The form reader attempts to interpret the submitted text.
outcomes: The reader accepts `blue` as a member of an assumed or externally supplied list.
The reader refuses `blue` because it is not in a different assumed list or because no list is available.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal.

open_points.subject: whole-number form parsing
open_points.question: Which textual forms count as a whole number, what numeric range and representation are required, and what refusal is required for invalid or out-of-range text?
options: Accept only unsigned base-10 canonical digits within a specified bound.
Accept signed base-10 integers, with a specified treatment of whitespace and leading zeroes.
Use the target language's integer parser and range.
open_points.default_guess: Accept trimmed unsigned base-10 digits, produce an arbitrary-precision nonnegative integer, and refuse every other form.

witness.initial: The release defines `count` as a whole-number field.
events: The form reader parses the text.
outcomes: The reader accepts `-1` as an integer.
The reader refuses `-1` because a whole number must be nonnegative.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal.

open_points.subject: yes-or-no form parsing
open_points.question: Which submitted texts represent yes and no, whether matching is case-sensitive or localized, and what refusal is required for any other text?
options: Accept only two canonical tokens defined by the release.
Accept a fixed set such as `yes`/`no` and common aliases.
Accept locale-dependent labels displayed by the owner interface.
open_points.default_guess: Accept only two release-defined canonical tokens and refuse all other text.

witness.initial: The release defines `enabled` as a yes-or-no field.
events: The form reader interprets the text.
outcomes: The reader refuses `true` because only `yes` and `no` are valid.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal.

open_points.subject: owner form submission completeness and multiplicity
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: May a defined field be omitted or submitted more than once, and what required result or refusal applies in each case?
options: Every defined field is required exactly once.
Every field is optional but may occur at most once.
Requiredness and multiplicity are additional release-owned facts for each field.
open_points.default_guess: Add release-owned requiredness and multiplicity facts and refuse submissions that violate them.

witness.initial: The release defines a field named `name`.
events: The owner submits no `name` entry, or submits two `name` entries.
The form reader validates the submission.
outcomes: The reader accepts the submission and treats the field as absent or keeps one occurrence.
The reader refuses the submission because the field is missing or repeated.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance versus refusal.

open_points.subject: unknown owner form fields
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What required outcome applies when a submission contains a name absent from the release's owner form table?
options: Refuse the entire submission.
Ignore unknown fields.
Preserve unknown fields as uninterpreted text.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the entire submission as inconsistent with the release-owned form table.

witness.initial: The release contains no field named `nickname`.
events: The form reader compares the name with the release table.
outcomes: The reader ignores or preserves `nickname` and accepts the submission.
witness.observer: The owner sees refusal versus acceptance or later sees the unknown value retained versus discarded.

open_points.subject: failure atomicity for owner form reading
open_points.question: When one submitted field cannot be read, must the entire form be refused without producing or applying any partial result, or may successfully read fields survive?
options: Refuse atomically and expose no partial interpreted result or effects.
Return successful values together with per-field failures.
Apply successful values and discard invalid fields.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse atomically and produce no partial result or effects.

witness.initial: A submission contains a valid text field and an invalid whole-number field.
events: The form reader processes the valid field before encountering the invalid field.
outcomes: The complete submission is refused and no interpreted values are applied.
The valid field is returned or applied while the invalid field alone is rejected.
witness.observer: The owner or a downstream record reader sees whether the valid field took effect.
